cities.base: Altstadt, for the arrival night and the last-night wind-down before the flight
cities.name: Zurich

cities.base: the valley floor itself, close to the cable car and train stations that run the whole region
cities.name: Lauterbrunnen

cities.base: old town near Chapel Bridge, gentler and prettier than people expect
cities.name: Luzern

cities.base: day trip only, reached via cable car from the Lauterbrunnen valley
cities.name: Mürren

cities.base: day trip only, the Top of Europe train from Lauterbrunnen
cities.name: Jungfraujoch

cities.base: day trip only, cogwheel and cable car combination from Luzern
cities.name: Mt. Pilatus

places.name: North Face Trail (Mürren to Gimmelwald)
places.note: An hour or so downhill along the cliff edge to the tiny hamlet of Gimmelwald, with the Eiger, Monch and Jungfrau north faces across the valley the whole way. Genuinely quiet.

places.name: Allmendhubel
places.note: Funicular up from the north end of the village, then a flat panoramic path back or a longer flower-trail loop in summer. Good for kids and for anyone who wants a view without a full hike.

places.name: Mürren village
places.note: Car-free, built on a shelf above the Lauterbrunnen valley. Quiet outside the cable car arrival times. Worth just sitting on a bench with the view rather than treating as a checklist item.

places.name: Schilthorn / Piz Gloria
places.note: Cable car from Mürren up to the revolving restaurant made famous by the Bond film. Views of the Eiger, Monch and Jungfrau without the Jungfraujoch crowds. Go up early before cloud builds.

places.name: Old Swiss House
places.note: Wood-paneled, old-fashioned, known for veal in the Zurich style. Pricier than it needs to be but a reliable sit-down dinner near the Lion Monument.

places.name: Hofkirche St. Leodegar
places.note: Twin-towered church above the lake with a well-known organ, a short walk past the Lion Monument. Quiet even when the bridge nearby is crowded.

places.name: Mt. Rigi
places.note: Queen of the Mountains, reached by cogwheel from Vitznau. Skip it on this itinerary, it scratches the same itch as Pilatus and you only have one Luzern mountain day to spend.

places.name: Mt. Pilatus (Golden Round Trip)
places.note: World's steepest cogwheel railway up from Alpnachstad, cable car down to Kriens, or reverse. Green and forested rather than glacial, a good contrast to the Jungfrau region, do not pair with Rigi on the same trip.

places.name: Jesuit Church (Jesuitenkirche)
places.note: Baroque interior right on the river, a two minute stop while crossing between the Chapel Bridge and the station side.

places.name: Sammlung Rosengart
places.note: Picasso and Klee, plus a strong Cartier-Bresson photography collection, in a manageable single building. The best indoor option if weather turns.

places.name: Verkehrshaus (Swiss Museum of Transport)
places.note: Trains, planes, a planetarium and a chocolate exhibit. Good rainy-day fallback if you have kids along, skippable otherwise since it eats half a day you don't really have.

places.name: Museggmauer (City Wall Towers)
places.note: Medieval wall with towers you can walk along and climb, open roughly April to November, closed in winter. Free, and gives you rooftop views over the old town without a cable car.

places.name: Lake Lucerne boat cruise
places.note: Boats leave from the pier by the train station, various loop lengths. Pleasant rather than essential, best used as the rain-day option instead of Pilatus.

places.name: Lion Monument (Löwendenkmal)
places.note: A carved dying lion in a quarry wall, mourning the Swiss Guard killed in 1792. Mark Twain liked it more than most modern visitors seem to. Fine if you're already passing, not worth a detour.

places.name: Luzern Altstadt (Old Town)
places.note: Painted facades on Hirschenplatz and Weinmarkt, easy flat walking, good arrival-afternoon activity with no ticket to buy.

places.name: Kapellbrücke (Chapel Bridge)
places.note: The wooden bridge and its water tower are the postcard image of Luzern, rebuilt after the 1993 fire so it is newer than it looks. Walk it once, don't linger.

places.name: Übriges Dörfli souvenir strip
places.note: The row of shops by the station selling cowbells and chocolate. Fine to glance at walking past, not worth allotting real time to.

places.name: Gimmelwald
places.note: Tiny cliffside hamlet below Mürren, a handful of wooden chalets and no real tourist infrastructure. Worth the short cable car detour precisely because nothing has been built up for visitors.

places.name: Talmuseum Lauterbrunnen
places.note: Small valley heritage museum, farming tools and old photographs. Fine for a rainy hour, not worth rearranging a clear-weather day for.

places.name: Schynige Platte
places.note: Rack railway up to an alpine garden and a long view down the valley toward the Jungfrau. Quieter alternative if Schilthorn or Jungfraujoch feel like too much crowd or too much cost, closed outside summer season.

places.name: Wengen
places.note: Car-free terrace village opposite Mürren, reached by train from Lauterbrunnen. A calmer alternative base and a fine wet-weather wander if the high ground is closed.

places.name: Kleine Scheidegg
places.note: Change point on the way to Jungfraujoch and the base of the Eiger's north face. Worth stepping outside here rather than staying glued to the train window.

places.name: Jungfraujoch (Top of Europe)
places.note: Highest train station in Europe, ice palace and glacier views. Spectacular when clear and a very expensive snack bar with white fog outside when not, check the webcam before committing and take the first train up.

places.name: Mürren village
places.note: Car-free village strung along a cliff edge, walkable down toward Grütschalp with the Jungfrau massif in view the whole way. Quiet in a way the bigger stops aren't.

places.name: Schilthorn / Piz Gloria
places.note: Panorama over the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau from the revolving restaurant deck. Fewer crowds than Jungfraujoch for a third the price, go early to beat afternoon cloud.

places.name: Trümmelbach Falls
places.note: Glacier meltwater roaring through the inside of the mountain via tunnels and lift. Cold and loud, worth the hour, skip it only if a bigger day is running long.

places.name: Staubbach Falls
places.note: Visible right from the village street, a short path climbs partway behind it. Five minutes is enough unless the light is good for photos.

places.name: Lauterbrunnen Valley floor walk (to Stechelberg)
places.note: Flat valley path past Staubbach Falls toward Stechelberg, 72 waterfalls on the valley walls, easy and free, good for the arrival afternoon before legs are needed for real climbing.

places.name: FIFA World Football Museum
places.note: Skip unless you're specifically a football fan. Pricey for what amounts to a corporate museum and it eats into the one day you have in the city.

places.name: Lindenhof
places.note: Small raised square on the site of a Roman fort, free view over the river and rooftops, locals playing chess at the tables. Two minutes off Bahnhofstrasse and nobody stops here.

places.name: Uetliberg
places.note: Zurich's home mountain, a 20 minute train from Hauptbahnhof then a short climb to a viewing tower over the city and lake, Alps behind on a clear day. Better use of a spare half day than another museum if the weather is good.

places.name: Kunsthaus Zurich
places.note: Strong Munch, Giacometti, and Monet holdings for a mid-size city museum. Worth it if weather turns and you actually have a spare afternoon, which on this itinerary you mostly don't.

places.name: Swiss National Museum (Landesmuseum)
places.note: Castle-like building right behind the main station, covers Swiss history from prehistory through the 20th century. Good rain-day option since it's an easy walk from the train.

places.name: Hiltl
places.note: Claims to be the oldest vegetarian restaurant in the world, pay-by-weight buffet is fast and good for a rushed lunch between train connections.

places.name: Zeughauskeller
places.note: Former armory turned beer hall, huge plates of Swiss classics like veal bratwurst and rösti. Loud and touristy but reliable and central for a jet-lagged first night.

places.name: Lake Zurich boat cruise
places.note: Short loop or a longer round trip toward Rapperswil. Pleasant filler on the last-afternoon-before-flight day, not essential if you've already done the Luzern boat.

places.name: Zurichsee lakefront promenade (Utoquai to Burkliplatz)
places.note: Flat lakeside walk with swans and Alps on the horizon on a clear day. Good decompression walk after a flight or before one.

places.name: Grossmünster
places.note: Twin-towered church tied to Zwingli and the Swiss Reformation, climb the tower for a city view over the river. Plain interior compared to Catholic cathedrals elsewhere, the point is the history and the climb.

places.name: Altstadt (Old Town) and Bahnhofstrasse
places.note: Narrow lanes on both sides of the Limmat, easy arrival-night walk after a long flight. Bahnhofstrasse itself is just an upscale shopping street, don't linger there.

places.name: Lauterbrunnen valley floor
places.note: The waterfalls-lined valley itself, the reason to sleep three nights here rather than pass through.

places.name: Lake Lucerne boat cruise
places.note: Pleasant, not essential, good if weather turns on your Luzern day.

places.name: Lion Monument
places.note: Skip unless you're already walking past it.

places.name: Chapel Bridge and the old town
places.note: Fine for an arrival-afternoon wander, skip the Lion Monument unless you're already walking past it.

places.name: Zeughauskeller
places.note: Straightforward Swiss dinner, about 30-35 CHF a head.

places.name: Altstadt and Bahnhofstrasse
places.note: Don't try to do Zurich properly, you don't have the days for it and that's fine.

places.name: Jungfrau Railway Tunnel Viewing Windows
places.note: The train stops briefly at the Eigerwand and Eismeer stations, both blasted into the rock face, where you can step out to windows cut into the mountainside. A strange piece of early 20th century engineering, five minutes each stop, don't wander off or you'll miss the train leaving.

places.name: Harder Kulm
places.note: Skip. A funicular up from Interlaken to a two-lake view, pleasant but redundant once you've done Schilthorn and Jungfraujoch, and Interlaken itself isn't in this itinerary as a base.

places.name: Grindelwald First
places.note: Skip on this itinerary. It's a legitimate day out with the cliff walk and the first flieger zipline, but it competes directly with the Schilthorn and Jungfraujoch days for time and money, and this trip doesn't have room for both regions properly.

places.name: Eiger Trail, Eigergletscher to Alpiglen
places.note: A real trail, about 6km and 3 hours, running directly beneath the north face of the Eiger with rockfall warning signs that are not decorative. Only do this if you're not exhausted from the summit already and the weather is holding. Ends at Alpiglen where you catch a train back down.

places.name: Eigergletscher Station
places.note: The changeover station on the way up, sitting right at the foot of the Eiger's north face. Worth stepping off here on the way down for a coffee and the view straight up the wall that killed climbers for decades before it was first summited.

places.name: Crystal Restaurant, Jungfraujoch
places.note: One of several cafeterias at the summit station, all overpriced by Swiss standards which is saying something. Bring your own sandwich if you'd rather not pay 20 CHF for a bowl of soup at 3,454 meters.

places.name: Lindt Swiss Chocolate Heaven
places.note: A chocolate shop and small exhibit at the summit station, free samples. Fine for filling ten minutes while waiting out weather, skip the overpriced gift boxes unless you're buying for someone specific.

places.name: Ice Palace
places.note: A tunnel of ice sculptures carved into the glacier itself, included with your ticket. Kitschy and a little cold-storage smelling, but it's fifteen minutes and gets you out of the wind.

places.name: Aletsch Glacier Snow Plateau Walk
places.note: A short walk out onto the edge of the longest glacier in the Alps, roped paths only. Snow underfoot year round, sunglasses matter more than people expect at this altitude.

places.name: Sphinx Observation Terrace
places.note: Reached by the fastest elevator in Switzerland, 108 meters in 25 seconds. On a clear day you see the Aletsch Glacier and into France and Germany. On a cloudy day you see fog. Cold and windy, bring a real jacket even in July.

places.name: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Station
places.note: The highest railway station in Europe, tunneled through rock since 1912. Take the first train up (book ahead) to beat the crowds that pile into the Sphinx observation deck by mid-morning. Check the webcam before you commit, cloud cover ruins the whole point of this.

places.name: James Bond World (Piz Gloria)
places.note: A small exhibit on the 1969 film 'On Her Majesty's Secret Service' shot here. Skip unless you're already at the summit waiting for a table or the weather to clear, it is a gift-shop-adjacent diversion, not a destination.

places.name: Piz Gloria revolving restaurant
places.note: The Bond-film restaurant, full rotation takes about 45 minutes. Food is average and priced for the view, but the 360 degree panorama over the Bernese Alps at that altitude is worth the one meal.

places.name: Stagerstubli
places.note: Small local restaurant in the village, cheese fondue and rosti, the kind of place you end up in on a rainy evening. Cash is useful, card not always taken.

places.name: Hotel Eiger terrace
places.note: Simple rosti and sausage lunch on a terrace facing the Jungfrau massif. Nothing fancy, the view does the work.

places.name: Mürren-Gimmelwald suspension bridge
places.note: Short pedestrian suspension bridge over the ravine, usually folded into the North Face Trail walk rather than visited alone.

places.name: Skyline Walk / Thrill Walk at Birg
places.note: A steel walkway bolted to the cliff face at the Birg mid-station, glass floor sections included. Included if you already hold a Schilthorn ticket. Skip if you dislike heights, there is no way to un-see the drop.

places.name: Schilthornbahn cable car (Stechelberg-Gimmelwald-Mürren-Birg-Schilthorn)
places.note: The lift system that makes the whole valley work. Note it's the same ride whether you're headed to Mürren for the night or up to the Schilthorn for the day, so no need to double pay if you plan it right with a pass.

places.name: Gimmelwald
places.note: Tiny farming hamlet below Mürren, reachable by the North Face Trail or cable car. A handful of houses and a mountain hostel. Nothing to 'do' here, that's the point.

outings.why: The highest-altitude train station in Europe and spectacular when clear, but 220 CHF for a snack bar with a view of white cloud if it's socked in.
outings.name: Jungfraujoch, Top of Europe
outings.season: June to September for the best odds of visibility
outings.fallback: Trümmelbach Falls, an hour inside the mountain regardless of weather.

outings.why: Cable car up to Piz Gloria with a walk down through Mürren if legs allow, views that rival Jungfraujoch for a third of the crowd.
outings.name: The Schilthorn, Piz Gloria
outings.fallback: Stay in Mürren and skip the walk down.

outings.why: A car-free village and a quiet descent, mostly free beyond a short cable car fare.
outings.name: Walk down through Mürren toward Grütschalp
outings.fallback: Ride the cable car straight down instead of walking.

outings.why: Glacier water falling through the inside of a mountain, skippable if the big mountain day runs long.
outings.name: Trümmelbach Falls

outings.why: Cogwheel up, cable car down, or reverse, gentler and greener than the Jungfrau region and a good contrast day.
outings.name: Mt. Pilatus golden round trip
outings.fallback: The Lake Lucerne boat cruise instead, 1-2 hours, about 40 CHF.

destination.name: Switzerland
destination.pitch: Three bases, one real mountain valley given three full nights, and the restraint to not chase six towns in eight days.
destination.caveat: There is no cheap version of this trip, and a cloud bank over the Jungfrau costs you 220 CHF with no refund and no do-over. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Zurich and Luzern give you one clean evening each of old-town walking without pretending to be the point of the trip.
because.food: Cheese, bread, and a Zeughauskeller dinner in Zurich cover it honestly rather than generously.
because.nature: The Lauterbrunnen valley and the peaks above it are the actual reason to come, not a day trip bolted onto a city stay.
because.culture: Luzern's old town and Chapel Bridge are a pleasant couple of hours, not a deep dive.
because.adventure: The Schilthorn and Jungfraujoch cable cars and cogwheels put you above 3000m without technical climbing.
because.exploration: Mürren's car-free quiet and the walk down to Grütschalp are the closest thing to getting off the marked path here.
